observed_symptoms.fact: Outage began when a network configuration change reached the spines of the 19 Multi-Colo PoP (MCP) data centers, taking them offline.
The 19 locations were about 4% of the network but their outage affected about 50% of total requests; egress bandwidth showed the same drop.
Withdrawal of site-local prefixes removed direct access to the locations and the servers' ability to reach customer origins.
Internal load balancer Multimog stopped forwarding between servers in the MCPs, so smaller compute clusters received the same traffic as large ones and overloaded.
Engineers had added difficulty reaching the affected locations to revert the change and used backup procedures to take control.
Not caused by an attack or malicious activity.

confirmed_root_cause.mechanism: While standardizing BGP communities attached to site-local prefixes, a change to the AGGREGATES-OUT prefix advertisement policy re-ordered terms so that the IPv4 and IPv6 site-local advertisement terms moved behind the explicit REJECT-THE-REST term. Site-local prefixes stopped being advertised (withdrawn) on the spines of MCP locations.
confirmed_elements: Change deployed to spines at 06:27, the first MCP-enabled location in the rollout
Term re-ordering placed site-local advertisement terms after an explicit reject term
Site-local prefix withdrawal cut origin reachability and disabled Multimog forwarding
contributing_factors: Stagger policy did not reach an MCP data center until its final step
Dry-run and peer review did not reveal the re-ordering; rollout steps were too large
Network engineers' overlapping reverts re-applied the bad change sporadically

investigation_evidence.evidence: Configuration diff on the spines showed exclamation-mark markers for re-ordered terms, with the site-local terms moved below REJECT-THE-REST.
First change made on a router to verify the root cause.
Root cause found and understood; work began to revert.
Successful HTTP requests and egress bandwidth graphs showed the impact scale.

recovery_actions.action: Began reverting the problematic prefix-advertisement policy change at affected locations, using backup access procedures where the network was unreachable.
Last revert completed, delayed because engineers reverted each other's reverts and re-introduced the fault sporadically.

recovery_verification.method: First data center brought back online.
All data centers online and working correctly after the final revert.

acceptable_alternatives.description: Revert the policy change at each affected location
Increase standby compute capacity in the affected PoPs
acceptable_alternatives.basis: Overload of smaller clusters is a secondary effect in the source, but capacity increase is not described as an action

acceptable_alternatives.description: Automated commit-confirm rollback, redesigned policy statement, MCP-aware staged rollout
acceptable_alternatives.basis: Listed as follow-up work, not used during recovery

not_stated_in_source: The exact telemetry or alert that first flagged the incident
Explicit post-revert verification tests beyond data centers being online

fixture_alignment.hypothesis_alignment: H02 is correct; the precise mechanism is term re-ordering behind an explicit reject, not an arbitrary incorrect policy.

A01.note: Capacity increase without restoring advertisements does not address the withdrawn prefixes.

A02.note: Roll back the policy and restore announcements.

A03.note: Superset of A02; the extra capacity step is not in the source.

A04.note: Modeled harmful action; the source does not describe it.

source_actions_missing_from_fixture: Backup access procedures to reach isolated locations
